title: Deciding to leave America: veterans' treatment and the Essex House refusal
summary: Seeing veterans denied jobs and being refused a room at the Essex House until a white companion booked it, he played a Princeton job for Red Allen and left for France.

Well, I always decided I was going back to Europe. I decided that because of what was happening at that time and I saw how things were running here in America.

I saw soldiers coming back and trying to get jobs that they were supposed to be getting and nothing was happening to them and the government was still doing what it was doing, and I was very touched by that.
So then, and the thing that touched it off one time I think I went to a -- I think it was a -- on 59th Street, The Essex House -- I'd just come into town and I said, I'd like to have a room.
And they said, well, we don't have any rooms. I said I don't want one for myself, but my friend would like to have a room. We don't have no rooms.

So, I went out and went into the car and said, you go on up and get the room, and she went in there and got a room right away. Right away. Then -- (inaudible) -- is this your policy? Did I read it right? He says, 'Well, ah, ah, ah, is she with you?' I says yes, oh, 'I didn't understand so I didn't pursue it any further but I said, this is it.'
Go. So -- right after, I played down in Princeton for -- Red Allen.
university -- and then I left. I'm on my way to France again.
